final_message:
DONE

I've built a 10-slide PowerPoint deck covering all four required analyses, ending with a summary slide of takeaways and recommendations. The charts are editable PowerPoint charts, and the totals match the workbook's own formulas (23.02 average days, $82,567 total cost). There was no slide-rendering tool on this machine, so I haven't seen the slides drawn; text fit is estimated from line lengths. Open the deck once to check the denser slides (scorecard, themes, data notes, summary).

**Headline findings**
- **Incidents per supplier:** 50 incidents across 12 suppliers, split evenly between 25 RMAs and 25 work orders. Aperion Defense has 10, Orionist Systems 9 and Velcronix 6. Each spreadsheet row counts as one incident; grouping lines from the same lot gives 33 distinct events.
- **Share of total:** those three suppliers make up 50% of all incidents. The deck shows this as a doughnut chart with a table.
- **Total cost:** $82,567 recorded. Work orders account for 94.9% of it. AeroNovus ($41,700), Viryonox ($18,250) and StratoSpacer ($12,000) together make up 87.1%.
- **Time to resolve:** 23.0 days on average (median 15.5). RMAs average 26.3 days (median 16, range 4–65) and work orders 19.7 days (median 15, range 2–61).
- **Recurring themes:** I grouped all 50 incident descriptions into five themes; the largest is MIL-STD or specification failures found at receiving (16 records). Defects found after receipt and packaging or handling damage account for 94.5% of cost. The AeroNovus ESD packaging failure ($41,700) was found in the warehouse, but whether the supplier or the warehouse caused it is not confirmed.

**Recommendations on the summary slide**
- **Supplier management:** corrective action requests for Aperion, Orionist and Velcronix; firmware checks before shipment for Viryonox; and better warranty and replacement-time terms for high-value assemblies.
- **Warehouse management:** an ESD audit, forklift and shelf-storage controls, a label check, and quarantining similar stock on the shelves when a defect is found.
- **Data and process:** make the cost, quantity and root-cause fields mandatory.

**Data problems, stated on a slide in the deck rather than corrected**
- **Partial year:** the workbook only covers January to July 2025, so this "annual" review is really year-to-date.
- **Missing costs:** 10 RMA records have no cost (all 9 Orionist records and 1 Velcronix). The $82,567 total is therefore a minimum.
- **Status conflict:** one KinextLink record is marked Open but has a close date. I included it, as the workbook does; without it the average is 22.9 days.
- **Wrong type:** a cable labeling error made by the warehouse team is logged as an RMA rather than a work order.
- **No registry:** there was no `workspace/` folder or registry, so I treated the reference workbook as the official record.

Files are in `outputs/`:
- `Inventory_Incident_Review_2025.pptx`
